To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated the first wireless 24-GHS roundtrip time-of-flight local-positioning frontend with an integrated RF transceiver, and that the performance of the self organizing localization network is evaluated using comparisons with reference trajectory.

a 24-GHz indoor positioning system using a low-cost CMOS radar frontend with a novel RF switching concept and an innovative distributed algorithm can achieve an absolute distance precision close to the theoretical limit and an absolute localization error of a few centimeters.
a 24-GHz radar transceiver can be used to achieve a localization accuracy in the centimeter scale in an indoor environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel localization system for indoor environments.
the design, implementation, and evaluation of a wireless indoor localization system using a distributed secondary radar network.
the development and integration of novel RF and signal processing techniques for a wireless indoor localization system based on a distributed network of radar nodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented system is the first to demonstrate that a truly wireless, low-cost, high-resolution, indoor localization system is feasible with 24-GHz radar technology.

the presented system is the first to achieve a truly wireless indoor localization network with centimeter accuracy, using 24-GHz radar transceivers and without requiring any additional infrastructure.
the system presented in this paper is a promising candidate to enable truly wireless, low-cost, low-power, and high-precision localization in indoor environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated a fully integrated CMOS radar transceiver with a novel receiver-transceiver switching concept that allows to operate the receiver and transmitter in a shared RF path without any significant degradation in performance.
we have shown a working system that is able to achieve centimeter localization accuracy with a very low power consumption of only 2.2 mW.
we have shown a working system that can be used to build an indoor localization network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

wireless localization can be achieved with a very low power budget using a low-cost, low-power CMOS transceiver, which makes the system suitable for a large number of nodes and a large number of users.
the presented system is a promising candidate for future indoor localization systems.
the presented system is the first to demonstrate a truly wireless 24 GHz round-trip time of flight local positioning system that operates in the 24-GHz band and is based on CMOS technology.
